surfaces.part: fumarole crack (glowing fissure lines on ground)

answer.evidence: The drawing is a thin Y/V-shaped crack with dark outline pixels and orange/red glowing fill, seen from above and lying flat on the ground. Silhouette widths are 2-10 px per row over rows 5-15, with no vertical face, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. Column scans show only 3-row runs (dark outline, bright orange, dark red) that are the crack's own shading, not a front face. This is a flat decal, which matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny orange zigzag of about 15x10 px on a plain background. It is smaller than one 16x16 tile, not the 4x3-tile ground patch the kind requires, and it has no surrounding ground surface at all. It has only 5 distinct colours and about 2 lightness steps (bright orange core, darker red edge), against 3 visible tones per tile for the grass and 7 for the paving. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, which points to a neutral dark outline rather than a tinted material tone, though at this size the evidence is thin. No grain, speckle or per-element shading is visible, so it reads as a sticker-like icon. The references carry dense grass tufts and individually shaded paving stones across full tiles. The candidate does not approach that richness or coverage.
